title: Do athletes with hamstring strain injury have shorter muscle fascicles in the injured limb?
journal: Journal of bodywork and movement therapies

sections.label: INTRODUCTION
sections.text: Previous studies have suggested that a reduced length of the biceps femoris long head (BF<sub>lh</sub>) fascicles may increase the risk of hamstring strain injury (HSI). However, it remains unclear whether the BF<sub>lh</sub> fascicles of the injured limb are shorter than those of the contralateral limb in athletes with an acute HSI.

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To investigate the between-limb asymmetry of BF<sub>lh</sub> fascicle length in amateur athletes with an acute HSI.

sections.label: METHODS
sections.text: Male amateur athletes were evaluated using ultrasound scans within five days following an HSI. The BF<sub>lh</sub> fascicle length was estimated using a validated equation.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Eighteen injured athletes participated in this study. There was no significant difference (p = 0.27) in the length of BF<sub>lh</sub> fascicles between the injured limb (9.53 ± 2.55 cm; 95%CI 8.26 to 10.80 cm) and the uninjured limb (10.54 ± 2.87 cm; 95%CI 9.11 to 11.97 cm). Individual analysis revealed high heterogeneity, with between-limb asymmetries (percentage difference of the injured limb compared to the uninjured limb) ranging from -42% to 25%. Nine out of the 18 athletes had a fascicle length that was more than 10% shorter in the injured limb compared to the uninjured limb, five athletes had a difference of less than 10%, and four athletes had a fascicle length that was more than 10% longer in the injured limb compared to the uninjured limb.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: The architecture characteristics of injured and uninjured muscles is not consistent among athletes with HSI. Therefore, rehabilitation programs focused on fascicle lengthening should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
